title: द्विचत्वारिंशत्तमोऽध्यायः
titleEn: Adhyaya 42 · The first clash of the two armies

summary.en: Dhritarashtra asks who struck first, and Sanjaya names the Kaurava and Pandava leaders drawn up face to face. The great armies advance on each other and the battle begins.
summary.kn: ಮೊದಲು ಯಾರು ಹೊಡೆದರೆಂದು ಧೃತರಾಷ್ಟ್ರ ಕೇಳುತ್ತಾನೆ; ಸಂಜಯನು ಮುಖಾಮುಖಿ ನಿಂತ ಕೌರವ, ಪಾಂಡವ ನಾಯಕರನ್ನು ಹೆಸರಿಸುತ್ತಾನೆ. ಮಹಾಸೈನ್ಯಗಳು ಎದುರಾಗಿ ನುಗ್ಗುತ್ತವೆ, ಯುದ್ಧ ಶುರುವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.
summary.hi: धृतराष्ट्र पूछते हैं कि पहले किसने प्रहार किया, और संजय आमने-सामने खड़े कौरव-पाण्डव नायकों के नाम बताते हैं। दोनों विशाल सेनाएँ एक-दूसरे पर बढ़ती हैं और युद्ध आरम्भ होता है।
summary.te: ముందుగా ఎవరు కొట్టారని ధృతరాష్ట్రుడు అడుగుతాడు; ఎదురెదురుగా నిలిచిన కౌరవ, పాండవ నాయకులను సంజయుడు పేర్కొంటాడు. మహాసేనలు ఒకదానిపై ఒకటి దూకి యుద్ధం మొదలవుతుంది.
summary.ta: முதலில் தாக்கியவர் யார் என்று த்ருதராஷ்டிரன் கேட்கிறான்; எதிரெதிரே நிற்கும் கௌரவ பாண்டவத் தலைவர்களைச் சஞ்சயன் பெயரிடுகிறான். பெரும்படைகள் ஒன்றை ஒன்று தாக்க, போர் தொடங்குகிறது.
summary.ml: ആരാണ് ആദ്യം പ്രഹരിച്ചതെന്ന് ധൃതരാഷ്ട്രർ ചോദിക്കുന്നു; കൗരവ, പാണ്ഡവ നേതാക്കൾ മുഖാമുഖം അണിനിരന്നത് സഞ്ജയൻ പറയുന്നു. മഹാസേനകൾ പരസ്പരം അടുക്കുന്നു, യുദ്ധം തുടങ്ങുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 6.42; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Mon Jul 26 2021

verses.text: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच

meaning.en: Dhritarashtra said:

verses.text:
एवं व्यूढेष्वनीकेषु मामकेष्वितरेषु च ।
के पूर्वं प्राहरंस्तत्र कुरवः पाण्डवास्तथा ॥

meaning.en: When the armies, mine and the others, had been drawn up like this, who struck first there, the Kauravas or the Pandavas?

verses.text: संजय उवाच

meaning.en: Sanjaya said:

verses.text:
भ्रातृभिः सहितो राजन्पुत्रो दुर्योधनस्तव ।
भीष्मं प्रमुखतः कृत्वा प्रययौ सह सेनया ॥

meaning.en: Your son Duryodhana, together with his brothers, advanced with his army, placing Bhishma at the front.

verses.text:
तथैव पाण्डवाः सर्वे भीमसेनपुरोगमाः ।
भीष्मेण युद्धमिच्छन्तः प्रययुर्हृष्टमानसाः ॥

meaning.en: In the same way all the Pandavas, led by Bhimasena, advanced in high spirits, wanting to fight Bhishma.

verses.text:
क्ष्वेडाः किलकिलाशब्दाः क्रकचा गोविषाणिकाः ।
भेरीमृदङ्गमुरजा हयकुञ्जरनिस्वनाः ॥

meaning.en: There were war cries and shouts, cymbals and cowhorns, kettledrums, mridangas and muravas, and the noise of horses and elephants.

verses.text:
उभयोः सेनयो राजंस्ततस्तेऽस्मान्समाद्रवन् ।
वयं प्रतिनदन्तश्च तदासीत्तुमुलं महत् ॥

meaning.en: Then, O king, the troops of both armies rushed at one another, and we answered with roars, and a great tumult arose.

verses.text:
महान्त्यनीकानि महासमुच्छ्रये
समागमे पाण्डवधार्तराष्ट्रयोः ।
चकम्पिरे शङ्खमृदङ्गनिस्वनैः
प्रकम्पितानीव वनानि वायुना ॥

meaning.en: At the meeting of the Pandavas and Dhritarashtra's sons, the mighty armies, towering high, shook with the sound of conches and drums, like forests shaken by the wind.

verses.text:
नरेन्द्रनागाश्वरथाकुलाना-
मभ्यायतीनामशिवे मुहूर्ते ।
बभूव घोषस्तुमुलश्चमूनां
वातोद्धुतानामिव सागराणाम् ॥

meaning.en: As those hosts, crowded with kings, elephants, horses and chariots, charged in that inauspicious hour, their uproar was like that of oceans lashed by wind.

verses.text:
तस्मिन्समुत्थिते शब्दे तुमुले लोमहर्षणे ।
भीमसेनो महाबाहुः प्राणदद्गोवृषो यथा ॥

meaning.en: When that terrifying, hair-raising din arose, mighty-armed Bhimasena bellowed like a bull.

verses.text:
शङ्खदुन्दुभिनिर्घोषं वारणानां च बृंहितम् ।
सिंहनादं च सैन्यानां भीमसेनरवोऽभ्यभूत् ॥

meaning.en: Bhimasena's roar overwhelmed the blast of conches and drums, the trumpeting of elephants and the lion-roars of the troops.

verses.text:
हयानां हेषमाणानामनीकेषु सहस्रशः ।
सर्वानभ्यभवच्छब्दान्भीमसेनस्य निस्वनः ॥

meaning.en: His cry drowned out all the sounds of thousands of neighing horses in the ranks.

verses.text:
तं श्रुत्वा निनदं तस्य सैन्यास्तव वितत्रसुः ।
जीमूतस्येव नदतः शक्राशनिसमस्वनम् ॥

meaning.en: Hearing that roar, like the thunder of a rumbling cloud with the crash of Indra's bolt, your troops trembled.

verses.text:
वाहनानि च सर्वाणि शकृन्मूत्रं प्रसुस्रुवुः ।
शब्देन तस्य वीरस्य सिंहस्येवेतरे मृगाः ॥

meaning.en: All the animals voided dung and urine at the sound of that hero, as other beasts do at a lion.

verses.text:
दर्शयन्घोरमात्मानं महाभ्रमिव नादयन् ।
विभीषयंस्तव सुतांस्तव सेनां समभ्ययात् ॥

meaning.en: Showing his dreadful form and making the sky resound like a great cloud, he rushed on your army, terrifying your sons.

verses.text:
तमायान्तं महेष्वासं सोदर्याः पर्यवारयन् ।
छादयन्तः शरव्रातैर्मेघा इव दिवाकरम् ॥

meaning.en: As that great archer came on, your sons, his brothers, surrounded him, covering him with swarms of arrows as clouds cover the sun.

verses.text:
दुर्योधनश्च पुत्रस्ते दुर्मुखो दुःसहः शलः ।
दुःशासनश्चातिरथस्तथा दुर्मर्षणो नृप ॥

meaning.en: They were your son Duryodhana, Durmukha, Duhsaha, Shala, Duhshasana, the great chariot-fighter, and Durmarshana, O king,

verses.text:
विविंशतिश्चित्रसेनो विकर्णश्च महारथः ।
पुरुमित्रो जयो भोजः सौमदत्तिश्च वीर्यवान् ॥

meaning.en: Vivimshati, Chitrasena, the great warrior Vikarna, Purumitra, Jaya, Bhoja, and the mighty son of Somadatta.

verses.text:
महाचापानि धुन्वन्तो जलदा इव विद्युतः ।
आददानाश्च नाराचान्निर्मुक्ताशीविषोपमान् ॥

meaning.en: They twanged their great bows like clouds flashing lightning, and took up iron arrows that flew like venomous snakes let loose.

verses.text:
अथ तान्द्रौपदीपुत्राः सौभद्रश्च महारथः ।
नकुलः सहदेवश्च धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पार्षतः ॥

meaning.en: Then the sons of Draupadi, the great chariot-fighter son of Subhadra, Nakula and Sahadeva, and Dhrishtadyumna, son of Prishata,

verses.text:
धार्तराष्ट्रान्प्रतिययुरर्दयन्तः शितैः शरैः ।
वज्रैरिव महावेगैः शिखराणि धराभृताम् ॥

meaning.en: went against Dhritarashtra's sons, tormenting them with sharp arrows, as swift thunderbolts hammer the peaks of mountains.

verses.text:
तस्मिन्प्रथमसंमर्दे भीमज्यातलनिस्वने ।
तावकानां परेषां च नासीत्कश्चित्पराङ्मुखः ॥

meaning.en: In that first crush, with the sound of Bhima's bowstring slapping his guard, no one among your men or the enemy turned his face away.

verses.text:
लाघवं द्रोणशिष्याणामपश्यं भरतर्षभ ।
निमित्तवेधिनां राजञ्शरानुत्सृजतां भृशम् ॥

meaning.en: I saw, best of the Bharatas, the quickness of Drona's pupils as they loosed arrows again and again, hitting any target they chose.

verses.text:
नोपशाम्यति निर्घोषो धनुषां कूजतां तथा ।
विनिश्चेरुः शरा दीप्ता ज्योतींषीव नभस्तलात् ॥

meaning.en: The din of twanging bows never ceased, and blazing arrows flew out like stars from the sky.

verses.text:
सर्वे त्वन्ये महीपालाः प्रेक्षका इव भारत ।
ददृशुर्दर्शनीयं तं भीमं ज्ञातिसमागमम् ॥

meaning.en: All the other kings, O Bharata, watched like spectators that fearsome meeting of kinsmen.

verses.text:
ततस्ते जातसंरम्भाः परस्परकृतागसः ।
अन्योन्यस्पर्धया राजन्व्यायच्छन्त महारथाः ॥

meaning.en: Then, seething with rage, each blaming the other for wrongs done, those great chariot-warriors strove against each other in rivalry, O king.

verses.text:
कुरुपाण्डवसेने ते हस्त्यश्वरथसंकुले ।
शुशुभाते रणेऽतीव पटे चित्रगते इव ॥

meaning.en: The Kuru and Pandava armies, crowded with elephants, horses and chariots, shone brilliantly in the battle, like a painted canvas.

verses.text:
ततस्ते पार्थिवाः सर्वे प्रगृहीतशरासनाः ।
सहसैन्याः समापेतुः पुत्रस्य तव शासनात् ॥

meaning.en: Then all those kings, bows in hand, charged together with their troops on your son's command.

verses.text:
युधिष्ठिरेण चादिष्टाः पार्थिवास्ते सहस्रशः ।
विनदन्तः समापेतुः पुत्रस्य तव वाहिनीम् ॥

meaning.en: And thousands of kings, directed by Yudhishthira, roaring, charged against your son's army.

verses.text:
उभयोः सेनयोस्तीव्रः सैन्यानां स समागमः ।
अन्तर्धीयत चादित्यः सैन्येन रजसावृतः ॥

meaning.en: The clash of the two armies was fierce, and the sun was hidden, veiled by the dust raised by the troops.

verses.text:
प्रयुद्धानां प्रभग्नानां पुनरावर्ततामपि ।
नात्र स्वेषां परेषां वा विशेषः समजायत ॥

meaning.en: As men attacked, broke, and rallied again, no difference could be seen between one's own side and the enemy's.

verses.text:
तस्मिंस्तु तुमुले युद्धे वर्तमाने महाभये ।
अति सर्वाण्यनीकानि पिता तेऽभिव्यरोचत ॥

meaning.en: In that tumultuous, terrifying battle, your father Bhishma stood out brilliantly above all the divisions.
